events.title: Agnes of Poitou and Andrew I of Hungary negotiate their border
events.description: Agnes of Poitou, regent of the Holy Roman Empire for her son Henry IV, met King Andrew I of Hungary to negotiate the border in the area of Burgenland. It remained the western frontier of medieval Hungary until the 16th century.
events.html: Agnes of Poitou, regent of the Holy Roman Empire for her son Henry IV, met King Andrew I of Hungary to negotiate the border in the area of Burgenland. It remained the western frontier of medieval Hungary until the 16th century.

events.title: Harald Hardrada and Tostig defeat Edwin and Morcar at Fulford
events.description: Harald Hardrada, King of Norway, and his English ally Tostig Godwinson defeated the northern earls Edwin and Morcar at Fulford, south of York, in his bid for the English throne. Harald and Tostig were both killed at Stamford Bridge that year.

events.title: Saladin begins the siege of Jerusalem
events.description: Saladin's army arrived before Jerusalem, held by the crusaders for 88 years. Balian of Ibelin surrendered the city twelve days later, and most inhabitants were allowed to ransom themselves.
events.html: Saladin's army arrived before Jerusalem, held by the crusaders for 88 years. Balian of Ibelin surrendered the city twelve days later, and most inhabitants were allowed to ransom themselves.

events.title: Prince Louis of France renounces his claim to the English throne
events.description: Prince Louis of France, proclaimed King of England by rebel barons, ratified the Treaty of Lambeth after defeats at Lincoln, Dover and Sandwich, ending the First Barons' War. He was paid 10,000 marks and pledged never to invade England again.

events.title: The Great Prussian Uprising against the Teutonic Knights begins
events.description: Encouraged by the defeat of the Livonian Order and Teutonic Knights at Durbe, the Old Prussians rose against the Teutonic Order, each clan choosing its own leader, such as Herkus Monte of the Natangians. The knights crushed the revolt by 1274.

events.title: Robert of Geneva is elected Clement VII, beginning the Western Schism
events.description: Cardinals who opposed Pope Urban VI elected Robert of Geneva as Clement VII, the first antipope to reside in Avignon. Rival popes in Rome and Avignon, and from 1409 a third line from Pisa, claimed the papacy until 1417.
events.html: Cardinals who opposed Pope Urban VI elected Robert of Geneva as Clement VII, the first antipope to reside in Avignon. Rival popes in Rome and Avignon, and from 1409 a third line from Pisa, claimed the papacy until 1417.

events.title: Magellan sets sail to find a western route to the Spice Islands
events.description: Ferdinand Magellan left Sanlúcar de Barrameda with five ships and about 270 men. He was killed in the Philippines, but one ship returned in 1522, completing the first voyage round the world.
events.html: Ferdinand Magellan left Sanlúcar de Barrameda with five ships and about 270 men. He was killed in the Philippines, but one ship returned in 1522, completing the first voyage round the world.

events.title: Italian troops breach the walls of Rome at Porta Pia
events.description: After French troops left Rome, Italian forces broke through the walls and took the city. The Papal States ended, and Rome became the capital of united Italy the following year.
events.html: After French troops left Rome, Italian forces broke through the walls and took the city. The Papal States ended, and Rome became the capital of united Italy the following year.

events.title: Billie Jean King beats Bobby Riggs in the 'Battle of the Sexes'
events.description: Before some 30,000 spectators in Houston and a huge TV audience, Billie Jean King beat former champion Bobby Riggs in straight sets. The match became a landmark for women's sport.
